_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for Phase 0 of the Shop roadmap (the shared Payments extension), rendered at /extensions/shop/roadmap. Task status is maintained by `npm run roadmap:payments` (scripts/gen-roadmap.mjs) from the extension source tree.

milestones.title: Phase 0a · The payments core
milestones.goal: One shared Payments extension, hidden from the Extensions list and switched on the first time any feature needs to take money.

tasks.title: One provider interface, many payment methods
tasks.detail: The Membership and Forms gateway classes merged into one. Each provider (Stripe, PayPal, a local provider) is written once and reports the methods it offers for the shop's country and currency, so checkout shows each customer only what fits their order. It covers starting a payment, confirming it from a return or a webhook, payments that wait (bank transfer, over-the-counter cash), refunds, and recurring charges where the method allows them.

tasks.title: Hidden, and switched on only when money is taken
tasks.detail: Payments does not appear in the Extensions list and no extension requires it. It is installed and turned on the first time a feature needs it: selling switched on in Shop, the Payments module in Membership, a Take payment action in a form, a deposit on a booking. A catalog-mode shop, a free members site or a contact form never loads it. Once on, it adds one Payments screen for keys, the ledger, invoices, tax and coupons, and it stays installed because it holds the payment records.

tasks.title: Stripe, PayPal and pay later: one-off payments
tasks.detail: Cards and wallets through Stripe, PayPal, and bank transfer or pay on collection, set up once in one settings screen for the whole site. Full and part refunds, sent back through the provider where it can.

tasks.title: One payments ledger
tasks.detail: Every payment and refund from every extension in one table, each tagged with what it paid for (an order, a plan, a form entry, a booking), with a history of everything that happened to it and a webhook address per provider.

milestones.title: Phase 0b · Everything that sells moves onto it
milestones.goal: Forms and Membership each carry their own Stripe, PayPal, offline gateways and coupons. Each gets a switch to the shared core for new purchases, while what already renews stays where it is.

tasks.title: Recurring payments
tasks.detail: Subscriptions on the shared core: start, renew, fail and retry, pause, switch price, cancel at the end of the period, with each method saying whether it can charge again.

tasks.title: Invoices and tax
tasks.detail: Numbered invoices and tax by country from the one ledger, with the tax report.

tasks.title: One coupon engine
tasks.detail: Fixed and percentage codes with limits on uses, dates, customers and what they apply to (products, categories, plans, forms), so one code can work across the store and the memberships.

tasks.title: Membership can use it
tasks.detail: A “Payment system” choice in Membership: its own payment settings (the default) or the shared Payments system. Only new purchases follow the choice. Memberships that already renew stay where they are, so nobody is billed twice and switching back is safe.

tasks.title: Forms and Bookings can use it
tasks.detail: The same choice for paid forms, and through them booking deposits: new payments through the shared system, existing subscriptions left where they are.

tasks.title: The shared system becomes the default
tasks.detail: Once it has run on real sites: new installs start on the shared system, and each extension’s own provider settings are kept only for the subscriptions that still depend on them.

milestones.title: Phase 0c · Local payment methods
milestones.goal: One provider per region, each bringing its own methods.

tasks.title: Philippines: GCash, Maya and QR Ph
tasks.detail: The first new provider after the move, PayMongo: GCash, Maya, QR Ph, cards and bank transfers for shops in the Philippines.

tasks.title: Southeast Asia
tasks.detail: Xendit: e-wallets, QR payments, bank transfers, cards and over-the-counter cash across the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam in one provider.

tasks.title: More regions, as shops ask for them
tasks.detail: One provider per region, each a single file on the same interface: Mollie (Europe), Razorpay (India), Paystack and Flutterwave (Africa), Mercado Pago (Latin America), Square, and Dragonpay for online banking and cash payments in the Philippines.
